expect: pH 10 to 12 (p7.L13): aluminum hydroxides precipitate at lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides (beyond pH 6), from their different Ksp; then mixed with a lithium source and calcined in O2-rich environments above 600 °C (p7.L17-19)
question: Within what pH window must NFA hydroxide precursors be coprecipitated and why, and how are the precursors then turned into cathode powder?
rendered:
According to the document "Next-Generation Cobalt-Free Cathodes – A Prospective Solution to the Battery Industry's Cobalt Problem", the NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a pH window of 10-12. This is because hydroxides of aluminum start precipitating at a lower pH value when compared to hydroxides of nickel and iron, which precipitate beyond pH 6. This effectively narrows the coprecipitation window between 10 and 12 for the successful synthesis of NFA precursors in their hydroxide forms.

After coprecipitation, the outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed, and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors. Then, the NFA hydroxide precursors are mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) before calcination in an O2-rich environment at temperatures >600 °C. After calcination, the NFA cathode powders are cast into electrodes using a roll-to-roll slot-die coating process followed by cobalt-free LIB pouch cell assembly, formation, and cycling evaluation.
